title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
This incident illustrates an attempt to manipulate AI systems from the outside rather than from within their architecture. The method relied on flooding the web with high-volume, formally packaged text designed to pass as neutral research, on the assumption that language models absorb and reflect the sources they are trained on or retrieve from. The same study was cited hundreds of times across different articles, a technique intended to create artificial consensus in whatever data pipelines or retrieval systems the content might enter.

The failure mode this exposes sits in the sourcing layer of AI deployment. Chatbots that draw on web content or training corpora have no reliable mechanism to verify whether a publishing entity is a genuine institution, and volume and surface credibility can substitute for legitimacy. A human editorial check on sourcing provenance would be one point at which fabricated institutional identity might be caught, but that check is not standard in most retrieval-augmented or training pipelines at scale.

What is not established is whether the operation succeeded in measurably changing chatbot outputs, or whether any AI system can be shown to have reproduced the Hanover Institute's framing as a direct result of this content.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
# Summary

An Israeli-funded fake think tank called the Hanover Institute published over 560,000 words across 124 reports in nine days, designed to influence artificial intelligence chatbots to produce pro-Israel arguments. The website, which does not exist as a legal entity and has no named staff, presented Israel's positions on sensitive topics including Palestinian torture, war crimes, and starvation in Gaza as neutral research. The New York production company Piro Inc registered the operation with the US justice department as material distributed for the Israeli government under foreign agent disclosure laws.

The operation is part of a broader Israeli government campaign costing tens of millions of dollars routed through advertising company Havas Media to optimize content for AI systems. The strategy involves creating websites and content designed to appear in chatbot training data and responses, with some reports citing the same study over 450 times across different articles to shape how chatbots respond to Gaza-related questions. Israeli officials have expressed frustration that despite substantial spending on this public diplomacy effort, American public support for Israel has significantly declined, with recent polling showing 60 percent of Americans view Israel unfavorably.
